jobs.title: Data Operations Manager
jobs.excerpt: OverviewOverview:HealthEdge is looking for a Data Operations Manager with a focus on data insights who thinks like an engineer, works like a scientist and communicates like a strategist.
jobs.description:
Overview

Overview:

HealthEdge is looking for a Data Operations Manager with a focus on data insights who thinks like an engineer, works like a scientist and communicates like a strategist. This hybrid role sits at the intersection of data platform engineering and ITSM-aligned Problem Management – purpose-built to expose the hidden toil, technical debt and repeat failure patterns that drain engineering capacity and impact payer customer availability across our integrated platform of solutions.

You will leverage AI – including Claude and its supporting functions – to ingest disparate operational data sources, model failure trends and surface prioritized insights that drive permanent resolution rather than perpetual remediation.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Production stability is a business imperative for health plans that depend on HealthEdge solutions to process claims, manage care and engage members. Repeat incidents, unresolved technical debt and untracked toil create invisible drag on engineering velocity – and visible risk to client uptime. This role exists to make the invisible visible, and to turn data-driven findings into engineering action.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Operational Data Engineering

  • Design, build and maintain pipelines that consolidate data from PagerDuty, Jira, ServiceNow, Datadog, Splunk and other operational sources into a unified analytical layer.
  • Develop and curate data models that identify repeat incidents, known error patterns, chronic alert noise and engineering toil consuming disproportionate remediation cycles.
  • Maintain data quality, lineage and governance standards across all ingested sources – ensuring findings are defensible when presented to senior leadership.
  • Leverage AI and automation – including the Claude API and Claude-powered workflows – to accelerate pattern detection, root cause hypothesis generation and report synthesis across large operational datasets.

Problem Management Practice

  • Own and drive the Problem Management lifecycle across HealthEdge client-facing products.
  • Translate incident patterns into structured Problem Records with defined scope, impact quantification, and recommended permanent fix strategies.
  • Partner with Engineering, SRE, Platform and Product teams to embed problem-driven prioritization into sprint planning and tech debt roadmaps.
  • Facilitate Problem Review sessions – leading cross-functional teams from data to decision
  • Define and track KPIs that demonstrate Problem Management value: reduction in repeat SEV1/SEV2 incidents, MTTR improvement, tech debt resolution velocity and engineering hours reclaimed from toil.

AI-Driven Insight & Visualization

  • Build interactive, executive-ready dashboards and data visualizations that make hotspots, failure modes and technical debt load immediately comprehensible to both engineering and business stakeholders.
  • Apply generative AI tooling to synthesize multi-source operational signals into clear, narrative-driven analysis – reducing time from data to decision.
  • Develop automated reporting workflows that surface trending issues and emerging risk patterns without requiring manual aggregation cycles.
  • Support monthly ceremonies by providing KPI and Outcome trending, highlighting influences to trending themes.

Stakeholder Communication & Business Translation

  • Present operational intelligence findings and Problem Management outcomes to Engineering leadership, VP-level+ audiences and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Influence from a strategic perspective where the most urgent pockets of risk to platform availability exist, and drive prioritization accordingly.
  • Translate technical findings – infrastructure failure modes, code regression patterns, dependency risks – into business value framing that drives prioritization conversations.
  • Author Problem Record summaries, trend analyses and executive briefings that are concise, evidence-based and action-oriented.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Technical Skills

  • 5+ years of data engineering experience with production-grade pipeline design, transformation logic and operational data modeling.
  • Proficiency with Python or Scala for data processing; strong SQL for analytical querying against large, event-driven datasets.
  • Hands-on experience with Jira and at least two of the following: PagerDuty, Datadog, Splunk, ServiceNow – ideally in an operational analytics or SRE context.
  • Experience integrating large language model (LLM) APIs – including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI or similar – into data workflows, automated summarization pipelines or insight generation applications.
  • Proficiency building interactive dashboards and data visualizations, Amazon Quick Suite a strong plus.

Operational & ITSM Knowledge

  • Working knowledge of ITIL or equivalent ITSM frameworks – specifically Incident Management, Problem Management and Change Management process disciplines.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify repeat failure patterns in incident or monitoring data and drive structured root cause analysis and resolution workflows.
  • Familiarity with SRE principles – toil quantification, error budgets, SLO/SLA measurement – and how engineering teams use these to prioritize reliability work.

Communication & Leadership

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated experience presenting technical analysis to VP or C-level audiences.
  • Ability to translate complex, multi-variable findings into business impact narratives that drive prioritization decisions.
  • Comfortable driving cross-functional alignment – navigating competing priorities across Engineering, Product, Operations and Leadership stakeholders.
  • Self-directed and intellectually curious; you pursue root causes with the same rigor you bring to your data models.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in a healthcare SaaS environment or regulated platform with high availability requirements.
  • Prior role embedded in an SRE, NOC, Platform Engineering or Operations function – particularly one that included formal Problem Management or post-incident review responsibilities.
  • Experience building AI-powered operational tooling – such as automated incident summarization, intelligent alert correlation or AI-assisted root cause classification.
  • Familiarity with HealthEdge products or the payer technology landscape is a meaningful plus.
  • ITIL Foundation certification or equivalent.

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, US

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

FLSA Classification (USA Only): Exempt

Work Environment: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: 

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work across multiple time zones in a hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Long periods of time sitting and/or standing in front of a computer using video technology.
  • May require travel dependent on company needs.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the job being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. HealthEdge reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Candidates may be required to go through a pre-employment criminal background check.

HealthEdge is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to workforce diversity and actively encourage all qualified persons to seek employment with us, including, but not limited to, racial and ethnic minorities, women, veterans and persons with disabilities.

**The annual US base salary range for this position is $130,000 to $140,000. This salary range may cover multiple career levels at HealthEdge. Final compensation will be determined during the interview process and is based on a combination of factors including, but not limited to, your skills, experience, qualifications and education.

jobs.description:
Per candidarsi, si prega di allegare il proprio CV aggiornato in lingua italiana

Chi siamo

In FutureLearn crediamo profondamente nel potere della formazione. Supportiamo studenti di tutto il mondo nel percorso di crescita professionale e investiamo concretamente nel loro futuro.

Siamo convinti che l’aggiornamento continuo rappresenti un investimento prezioso e aspiriamo ad aiutare le persone a prendere il controllo della propria carriera grazie a percorsi di apprendimento personalizzati basati in progressi concreti.

Collaboriamo con oltre 260 partner educativi di fama internazionale, tra cui prestigiose università, istituzioni globali e imprese di referenza nel rispettivo settore. Insieme, offriamo alla nostra community di oltre 20 milioni di studenti accesso a corsi e programmi di laurea online, flessibili e di alta qualità.

Mission

Non ci limitiamo a insegnare nuove competenze: vogliamo contribuire a processi di trasformazione individuale. FutureLearn è alla ricerca di persone che condividano la nostra passione per l’apprendimento continuo, l’emancipazione professionale e un’istruzione accessibile a tutti.

Cosa stiamo cercando

L’Admissions Officer – Italia è responsabile della gestione e valutazione delle candidature per i programmi di Laurea e Post-laurea, garantendo che ogni domanda sia valutata in modo accurato, coerente e conforme ai requisiti di ammissione.

Questo ruolo prevedere la verifica dei requisiti accademici e della documentazione italiana e internazionale dei candidati ai master. L’admission Officer si occuperà della valutazione dei titoli di studio, inclusi quelli esteri e la relativa documentazione CIMEA, e della gestione delle ammissioni degli studenti.

Il ruolo richiede una buona conoscenza del sistema di Istruzione Superiore italiano, ottime capacità organizzative e analitiche, attenzione ai dettagli e capacità di gestire un elevato volume di candidature rispettando scadenze e priorità. La persona collaborerà con Student Recruitment e con gli altri stakeholder interni per garantire un processo di candidatura e immatricolazione efficiente.

Principali responsabilità

  • Gestire e valutare le candidature secondo le policy di ammissione e i requisiti specifici dei programmi.

  • Verificare i requisiti accademici, professionali e linguistici dei candidati.

  • Valutare titoli di studio italiani e internazionali e la relativa documentazione, inclusi certificati, transcript e Diploma Supplement.

  • Valutare, secondo le procedure stabilite, la documentazione relativa ai titoli di studio esteri, inclusi gli attestati CIMEA di Comparabilità e/o Verifica, ove applicabili.

  • Verificare la completezza, coerenza e autenticità della documentazione e richiedere eventuali integrazioni.

  • Gestire le decisioni di ammissione e l’emissione delle relative offerte, nell’ambito delle proprie responsabilità.

  • Registrare e mantenere aggiornati i dati e la documentazione nei CRM, nelle piattaforme di application e nei sistemi gestionali.

  • Gestire un elevato volume di candidature, garantendo il rispetto delle scadenze degli intake.

  • Collaborare con Student Recruitment e gli altri team interni per risolvere problematiche relative alle candidature e garantire un processo efficiente.

  • Monitorare le candidature, identificare eventuali criticità e segnalare all’Admissions Manager.

  • Mantenere aggiornate le proprie conoscenze sulle policy di ammissione, sui requisiti dei programmi e sulle procedure dell’istituzione.

  • Contribuire al miglioramento continuo dei processi di Admissions.

  • Garantire la corretta gestione dei dati personali e accademici nel rispetto del GDPR.

  • Fornire aggiornamenti regolari all’Admissions Manager su carichi di lavoro, candidature e casi aperti.

Competenze, conoscenze ed esperienza – Requisiti essenziali

  • Esperienza professionale nel settore Admissions, preferibilmente in ambito Higher Education.

  • Esperienza nella gestione di candidature di studenti italiani e internazionali.

  • Buona conoscenza del sistema italiano dell’Istruzione Superiore e della relativa terminologia.

  • Esperienza nella valutazione di titoli accademici e della documentazione necessaria per l’ammissione.

  • Esperienza nella valutazione di titoli di studio esteri e conoscenza dei relativi processi di verifica.

  • Conoscenza pratica della documentazione e dei processi CIMEA, ove applicabili.

  • Capacità di interpretare e applicare correttamente policy e requisiti di ammissione.

  • Elevata attenzione ai dettagli e capacità di individuare discrepanze o informazioni mancanti.

  • Ottime capacità analitiche, decisionali e di problem solving.

  • Esperienza nell’utilizzo di CRM, piattaforme di application o Student Records Systems.

  • Ottime capacità organizzative e capacità di gestire elevati volumi di lavoro e scadenze.

  • Ottime capacità di comunicazione in italiano e inglese.

  • Capacità di lavorare efficacemente in un ambiente internazionale e multiculturale.

  • Buona conoscenza di Microsoft Office.

  • Elevato livello di riservatezza e attenzione nella gestione dei dati personali e accademici.

Competenze, conoscenze ed esperienza – Requisiti preferenziali

  • Laurea triennale o titolo di studio equivalente.

  • Esperienza specifica nelle Admissions di programmi

  • Esperienza presso un’università italiana, istituzione di Higher Education o education provider.

  • Esperienza nella valutazione di titoli internazionali provenienti da diversi Paesi.

  • Esperienza con CIMEA-Diplome e relativa documentazione.

  • Conoscenza della normativa e delle procedure italiane relative all’ammissione agli studi universitari.

  • Esperienza nella gestione di candidature per più università o partner accademici.

  • Esperienza in un ambiente di Higher Education online, distance learning o internazionale.

  • Esperienza nell’utilizzo di Salesforce o altri CRM.

  • Buona conoscenza di Excel e capacità di analizzare dati e produrre report.

  • Conoscenza del GDPR applicato al settore Higher Education.

  • La conoscenza di ulteriori lingue straniere sarà considerata un plus.

Cosa offriamo

  • Contratto full‑time a tempo indeterminato.

Summary

As an Implementation Consultant (Carbon Accounting) at Workiva, you’ll implement Workiva Carbon for clients and help them build credible greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions accounting programs. You’ll also bring client feedback back to those teams to improve the product and our delivery approach.


What You’ll Do


  • Support or conduct discovery sessions to understand client emissions inventories, data sources, and reporting requirements
  • Configure and implement Workiva Carbon, including data mapping, activity data ingestion, emission factor selection, calculating emissions, and reporting.
  • Advise clients on Scope 1, 2, and 3 accounting under the GHG Protocol
  • Support clients in aligning emissions metrics with frameworks and regulations such as CDP, CSRD/ESRS, SB 253/261, GRI, SASB, TCFD, and ISSB
  • Support client audit and assurance readiness by documenting methodologies and data sources
  • Create process documentation and train client users
  • Test, troubleshoot, and document issues; escalate to Product and Engineering
  • Manage assigned workstreams to scope, hours, and deadlines

  • Collaborate with Sustainability Reporting teammates on combined Carbon and reporting implementations, with opportunity to lead as you grow

What You'll Need


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 4+ years of experience in GHG accounting (Scope 1, 2, and 3) under the GHG Protocol

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in consulting, software implementation, or service delivery
  • Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills

  • Public accounting, audit, or assurance background

Travel Requirements and Working Conditions

Workiva is the platform designed to bring confidence, control, and a competitive edge to the world’s most complex organizations. If you’re energized by meaningful challenges, inspired by collaborative teams, and motivated to help organizations turn uncertainty into advantage, we’d love to meet you.

Workiva is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that great minds think differently. We value diversity of backgrounds, beliefs, and interests, and we recognize diversity as an important source of intellectual thought, varied perspective, and innovation. Employment decisions are made without regard to age, gender identity, race, religion, disability status, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.

Workiva is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. To request assistance with the application process, please email .

Workiva employees are required to undergo comprehensive security and privacy training tailored to their roles, ensuring adherence to company policies and regulatory standards.

Workiva supports employees in working where they work best - either from an office or remotely from any location within their country of employment.

jobs.description:
About the role

Terabase Energy builds digital and automation tools for utility-scale solar, spanning robotic field construction (Terafab), EPC services (Construct), plant design and energy modeling (PlantPredict), SCADA, and related services.

The Lead Financial Analyst is the finance business partner across these product lines, owning forecasting, budgeting, and project performance analysis. The role builds AI-enabled reporting and analytics that turn project, operational, and system data into clear, decision-ready insight for leadership and business owners.

Key responsibilities

  • Forecasting and budgeting: Build and maintain the annual budget and rolling forecasts by product line, including revenue, COGS, OPEX, and headcount.
  • Project-level forecasting: Partner with Project Delivery, Sales, and Procurement teams to forecast active projects on a percent-complete basis and track margin by project and contract type.
  • Financial project management: Analyze project performance in depth over the full project term, including margin analysis and core margin drivers. Work with Project Delivery, Sales, Accounting, and IT to improve reporting and tracking processes, ensuring the data needed for meaningful performance analytics is available.
  • Finance business partner: Serve as the finance business partner to internal stakeholders, providing financial insight, decision support, and analysis that helps business leaders plan, prioritize, and manage performance.
  • Month-end close and variance analysis: Reconcile the P&L to NetSuite, validate GL and department mappings, and prepare actual-vs-forecast and actual-vs-budget variance analysis. Separate true performance variances from accounting reclassifications and timing, and explain the underlying drivers.
  • Intelligent reporting and analytics: Build and publish automated reporting and analytics for stakeholders, using AI tools and direct data feeds from core systems (NetSuite, Salesforce).
  • Process improvements: Define, document, and implement Finance processes end to end, including the forecast and budget cycles, month-end close, and cross-functional workflows with Project Delivery, Sales, Procurement, and Accounting. Set clear ownership, timelines, and controls, and drive adoption across teams.

Requirements

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 7–10 years of experience in FP&A, preferably including project-based financial management (EPC, construction, or long-term contracts).
  • Proven experience owning financial statements (P&L, Cash Flow).
  • Advanced data modeling and dashboarding of driver-based models with structured, auditable design.
  • Advanced experience applying AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) to financial analysis, reporting, and workflow automation.
  • Proven experience developing and implementing business processes.
  • Hands-on ERP experience (NetSuite preferred) with GL, department, and subsidiary structures.
  • Solid grasp of US GAAP revenue recognition, including percent-of-completion for long-term contracts.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to present findings to executives concisely.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in a start-up environment.
  • Experience in the energy and utility industry, EPC, or large-scale construction.
  • Background at a growth-stage or venture-backed company, including investor or board reporting.
  • Experience with Salesforce, Airtable, or BI tools (Tableau, Power BI).
  • Familiarity with mixed business models: hardware, software/SaaS, and services.
  • CPA, CFA, or MBA.

Within each posted range, individual pay is determined (and may be greater or higher), dependent on work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. • Generous time off and holiday policy

• Remote flexibility

• Flexible time off

• Comprehensive benefits package

• Career progression

• 401k match

• Stock options

Freight Dispatcher — Equipment & Freight Compatibility

Full-Time | Remote — United States | U.S. Freight Operations

Match the Freight to the Right Equipment

We are hiring a Freight Dispatcher — Equipment & Freight Compatibility to support U.S. trucking operations with a focus on equipment requirements, freight evaluation, load compatibility, trip planning, and dispatch coordination.

This position may be a strong fit for transportation professionals, including experienced or former CDL-A drivers, who understand that Dry Van, Reefer, Flatbed, and Step Deck equipment do not handle the same freight or operating requirements.

Previous employment specifically under the title of Freight Dispatcher is not required. Applicants must have relevant U.S. trucking, transportation, logistics, fleet, or closely related operational experience.

Equipment & Freight Compatibility

  • Review freight requirements before presenting available loads for consideration.
  • Determine whether assigned truck and trailer equipment is appropriate for the freight.
  • Review commodity information, cargo weight, dimensions, loading requirements, and applicable handling instructions.
  • Identify equipment requirements involving temperature control, cargo securement, tarping, dimensions, weight, or specialized loading procedures.
  • Recognize potential equipment and freight mismatches before a load is presented for approval.
  • Verify unclear equipment requirements with authorized transportation personnel.
  • Escalate freight requiring additional equipment, safety, or operational review.

Equipment Types

Applicants should understand the basic operating differences between:

  • Dry Van
  • Reefer
  • Flatbed
  • Step Deck

Knowledge of additional commercial equipment types is beneficial.

Freight Evaluation & Trip Planning

  • Use DAT One, Truckstop, or comparable U.S. freight load boards to review available freight.
  • Compare available loads by equipment requirement, lane, rate, mileage, appointments, and operating requirements.
  • Calculate loaded mileage, deadhead mileage, total trip mileage, and rate per mile.
  • Consider driver location, available Hours of Service, equipment configuration, pickup requirements, and delivery appointments.
  • Identify excessive deadhead, unrealistic schedules, equipment conflicts, or other operational concerns.
  • Present suitable freight options for authorized review and booking.
  • Negotiate freight rates only when specifically authorized.

Driver & Broker Communication

  • Communicate professionally with U.S. CDL-A drivers, freight brokers, shippers, receivers, and authorized transportation personnel.
  • Confirm freight and equipment requirements when assigned.
  • Clarify incomplete or inconsistent load information.
  • Communicate accurate freight and equipment information to drivers.
  • Confirm applicable pickup, delivery, loading, and operating instructions.
  • Escalate safety, compliance, broker-verification, documentation, equipment, or service concerns when appropriate.

Transportation Documentation

  • Maintain accurate load and dispatch records.
  • Review rate confirmations for freight and equipment information.
  • Maintain bills of lading, proof-of-delivery documents, and applicable transportation records.
  • Document applicable equipment requirements and shipment instructions.
  • Maintain accurate communication histories and operational notes.
  • Identify missing or inconsistent information requiring follow-up.

Required Transportation Background

Relevant professional experience may include:

  • CDL-A truck driving
  • Freight dispatch support
  • Fleet operations
  • Carrier operations
  • Transportation coordination
  • Logistics operations
  • Freight brokerage support
  • Load planning
  • Owner-Operator operations
  • Comparable U.S. trucking operations

Required Skills

  • Working knowledge of U.S. trucking and transportation operations.
  • Understanding of Dry Van, Reefer, Flatbed, and Step Deck equipment.
  • Ability to identify basic freight and equipment compatibility requirements.
  • Familiarity with U.S. freight load boards.
  • Understanding of cargo weight, dimensions, temperature requirements, and applicable securement considerations.
  • Understanding of pickup and delivery appointments.
  • Working knowledge of driver Hours-of-Service considerations.
  • Ability to calculate loaded mileage, deadhead mileage, total trip mileage, and rate per mile.
  • Fluent professional spoken and written English.
  • Strong professional telephone and email communication.
  • Strong attention to detail and accurate recordkeeping.
  • Computer and spreadsheet proficiency.
  • Reliable computer and stable high-speed internet connection.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Helpful Additional Experience

Experience with open-deck freight, temperature-controlled freight, cargo securement, specialized equipment, ELD systems, transportation-management systems, broker verification, active-load tracking, or freight documentation is beneficial.

Work Arrangement & Schedule

This is a full-time remote position supporting U.S. freight operations.

Hiring market: Remote — United States.

Qualified applicants may be considered throughout the United States.

Redwood Automation Solution Designer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance Close, Finland

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Finland. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

About Yadimen

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP finance close automation people in front of the client.

We're a growing healthcare company with several entities and clients across many US states, so no two weeks look the same. We're looking for someone who notices a gap next to their work and closes it—whether that's a filing deadline without an owner, a recurring travel question, or a spend report a director needs by Friday—with room to grow into cash forecasting and budget tracking as we scale.

Role Details:

  • Employment Type: Part-time Employee (approximately 16–20 hours per week)

  • Serve as a technical escalation point for complex programming, data, or deliverable issues, leading resolution of highly complex or ambiguous challenges.

jobs.description:
Redwood Automation Solution Designer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance Close, Hungary

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Hungary. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

About Yadimen

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP finance close automation people in front of the client.

We focus on delivering life-changing advances for individuals with genetic disorders not addressable with current approaches. For more information, please visit.

Position Details

Encoded is seeking an Associate Director, Development Program Manager to drive the cross-functional planning and execution of a development program within our AAV gene therapy platform, focused on central nervous system (CNS) indications. Reporting to the Director, Development Program Management, this role is for an experienced program management professional who combines strong organizational and project-management expertise with a solid understanding of the drug development process, ideally including gene therapy or other advanced modalities. The Associate Director will serve as the operational backbone for the program team, working closely with Research, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Patient Advocacy and Medical Affairs to ensure program timelines, budgets, risks, and deliverables stay aligned and on track, while partnering with and escalating to the Program Management Organization (PMO) Director on major risks, resourcing conflicts, and strategic trade-offs.

Program Strategy & Core Team Leadership

  • Organize Development Core Team activities that foster cross-functional collaboration, effective communication, and strategic discussion, ensuring all stakeholders are aligned on program objectives and milestones to aid decision-making
  • Ensure cross-functional teams are properly prepared for internal meetings, communications to management, and engagement with external partners

  • Track deliverables resulting from Core Team meetings, ensuring timelines are met and objectives are achieved
  • Identify program risks and dependencies early, and develop and track mitigation plans in partnership with functional leads, with particular attention to the specialized considerations of AAV gene therapy programs (e.g., viral vector supply timelines, long-term follow-up requirements, specialized dosing or delivery infrastructure for CNS administration)

  • Support scenario planning and contingency planning for key program decision points (e.g., go/no-go milestones, regulatory interactions, data readouts)
  • Contribute to the development and refinement of program management processes, templates, and best practices across the organization

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as the primary point of integration across functional areas for the program, ensuring consistent communication of program status, risks, and decisions
  • Partner with functional leads to coordinate cross-functional projects related to CMC, Regulatory, Clinical, Medical, Patient Advocacy, and Nonclinical, providing support and guidance to achieve project goals
  • Facilitate internal communication to identify risks and mitigations, escalating unresolved issues to the Director PM as needed

Budget & Resource Management

  • Partner with Finance and functional leads on budget forecasting
  • Support resource planning and capacity analysis across functions to ensure the program is appropriately staffed

Communication & Reporting

  • Monitor and report program progress, providing regular updates to cross-functional teams, the PM Director , and other stakeholders, highlighting key achievements, challenges, and mitigation plans
  • Utilize formal communication protocols and tools, including dashboards, reports, and weekly/monthly updates, to support company and operational goals
  • Support maintenance of program documentation in alignment with internal quality and compliance standards

Ad Hoc Projects

  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to contribute to ad hoc functional projects across various departments
  • Collaborate with team members to address challenges and find innovative solutions for ad hoc projects, as needed
  • Support Quarterly Business Review (QBR) and Board of Directors (BoD) meetings as needed
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a bachelor’s degree; or 6 years and a master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years' experience; or equivalent experience.
  • Advanced degree in life sciences, pharmacology, or a related field preferred; an MBA or project management certification is a plus
  • Demonstrated experience in program or project management within the biotech, pharmaceutical, or related life sciences industry
  • Working knowledge of the drug development process, including preclinical, clinical, regulatory, and commercial requirements
  • Experience supporting gene therapy, AAV vectors, or other advanced modality programs, and/or rare disease programs, strongly preferred
  • Proven track record of successfully leading and managing cross-functional teams in the development and execution of complex development programs, preferably in gene therapy
  • Up to 20% travel may be required

Skills and Attributes

  • Self-starter with the ability to work independently and take initiative
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage a complex, multi-functional program
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively at all levels of the organization
  • Strategic thinker with the ability to prioritize and make informed decisions in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong problem-solving abilities and a proactive, critical-thinking approach to identifying and resolving issues
  • Willingness to learn and collaborate in a dynamic team environment
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including experience preparing materials for and presenting to senior leadership
  • Proficient in Smartsheet, Office Timelines and/or other project management tools and software
  • Proven ability to evaluate existing PMO tooling, workflows, and delivery frameworks; skilled at identifying operational bottlenecks and providing strategic recommendations to modernize and streamline processes.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving company environment with the ability to adjust priorities as needed

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting rare disease or CNS-focused gene therapy programs
  • Familiarity with gene therapy–specific regulatory considerations
  • Demonstrated experience leveraging AI-assisted features within modern program and portfolio management tools to automate workflows, synthesize project data, and enhance team productivity.
  • Experience with governance processes in a biotech or pharmaceutical organization (e.g., portfolio reviews, stage-gate processes)
  • Familiarity with IND submission

jobs.description:
ABOUT STORD


Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.


By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.


With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.


Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like True Classic, Native, Seed Health, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

About the Role
The Regional Manager, Health, Safety, Compliance & Loss Prevention is responsible for executing and continuously improving Stord's HSS program across a defined region of fulfillment and warehouse facilities. Reporting to the Head of Health, Safety, and Security, this role translates enterprise standards into daily operational reality — driving consistent performance across sites, building regional team capability, and owning outcomes.

Regional Manager hires, develops, and directs a team of site-level safety and loss prevention professionals, holding them accountable to program standards while coaching them to grow. Success is measured by regional safety performance, loss prevention effectiveness, compliance posture, and the strength of the team built to sustain a culture.

What This Role Owns

Regional Managers are active partners in program design, governance, and policy-setting — contributing regional insight, operational context, and field intelligence to enterprise decisions led by the Head of HSS. They own translating those standards into consistent regional execution and are accountable for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that drive financial, operational, and asset loss across their region. The Regional Manager is accountable for:

  • Regional safety, compliance, and loss prevention performance metrics and trend improvement.
  • Translating enterprise standards into site-level execution — ensuring consistent, high-quality program delivery across every facility in the region.
  • Hiring, onboarding, and developing a regional team of HSS and loss prevention professionals.
  • Loss prevention strategy and shrink reduction for their region — including investigation oversight, security controls, and carrier/vendor accountability.
  • Regional compliance posture across OSHA, state regulations, and Stord internal standards.
  • Escalation management: serving as the regional decision-maker for incidents, investigations, and regulatory inquiries.
  • Risk ownership: proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks across the region that could result in financial loss, operational disruption, or damage to people and assets — before they become incidents.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Development

  • Recruit, hire, and onboard site-level safety and loss prevention professionals within the region.
  • Set clear performance expectations, conduct regular coaching conversations, and deliver structured feedback and development plans.
  • Build a high-accountability, growth-oriented team culture within the regional HSS function.
  • Identify talent gaps and succession needs; develop internal candidates for expanded roles.
  • Facilitate regional team meetings, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving across sites.

Safety Program Execution

  • Deploy and sustain enterprise safety standards across all regional facilities, ensuring consistent implementation.
  • Conduct or oversee facility safety audits, gap assessments, and corrective action tracking.
  • Support site leaders and operations teams in embedding safety into daily standard work and leadership routines.
  • Lead or oversee incident investigations within the region, ensuring root cause analysis quality and timely corrective action closure.
  • Represent the region in enterprise safety forums, surfacing trends, risks, and improvement opportunities to the Head of HSS.
  • Coordinate peak readiness reviews to ensure safety standards are maintained through volume surges and labor onboarding.

Loss Prevention and Asset Protection

  • Own regional loss prevention strategy, including shrink reduction targets, security controls, and investigative outcomes.
  • Oversee internal investigations related to theft, fraud, and inventory discrepancy — escalating to HR, Legal, or Law Enforcement as appropriate.
  • Analyze loss trends across the region and drive root cause resolution through operational and procedural improvements.
  • Manage CCTV, access control, and physical security standards across regional sites, partnering with facilities teams on remediation.
  • Build relationships with carrier partners, vendors, and law enforcement contacts to support loss prevention outcomes.
  • Partner with Operations and Finance to quantify and report on shrink, damage, and loss impact at the regional level.

Compliance and Regulatory Management

  • Ensure all regional facilities maintain compliance with applicable OSHA, state, and local regulations.
  • Serve as the regional point of contact for regulatory inspections, responding to inquiries and coordinating any required corrective actions.
  • Monitor regulatory changes with regional applicability and coordinate with the Head of HSS to update procedures accordingly.
  • Oversee Hazmat compliance within the region, including proper storage, labeling, training, and incident reporting.
  • Support site-level readiness for customer-required certifications such as GMP, GDP, CTPAT, or TAPA where applicable within the region.

Metrics, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

  • Own regional safety and loss prevention KPIs, delivering regular performance reporting to the Head of HSS and regional operations leadership.
  • Drive trend analysis across regional sites to identify systemic risks before they become incidents.
  • Manage corrective action pipelines within the region, ensuring timely closure and verified effectiveness.
  • Champion near-miss and hazard reporting culture across sites, tracking participation rates as a leading indicator.
  • Partner with Ops Excellence to integrate safety and loss prevention improvements into standard operating procedures.

New Site Launches and Network Changes

  • Lead HSS readiness for new site launches within the region, including safety walkthroughs, program onboarding, and staff training.
  • Support automation and equipment commissioning activities from a safety perspective within the region.
  • Ensure staffing and program coverage scales appropriately as the regional network grows.

Required Qualifications

Experience

  • 7+ years of experience in health and safety, loss prevention, or operations compliance.
  • 3+ years of direct people management experience, with a track record of hiring and developing high-performing teams.
  • Multi-site experience in 3PL, eCommerce fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated experience in loss prevention investigation, shrink management, or asset protection in a high-volume logistics or retail environment.

Technical Knowledge

  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards, state-specific safety regulations, and compliance program management.
  • Hands-on experience managing physical security systems, including CCTV, access control, and inventory protection protocols.
  • Familiarity with incident investigation methodologies and corrective action systems.
  • Comfort with Hazmat regulations and controlled substance handling requirements in a warehouse or fulfillment context.
  • Experience using safety and loss prevention data to drive operational decisions.

Credentials (Preferred)

  • ASP, CSP, or equivalent safety certification, or active pursuit of one.
  • Wicklander-Zulawski (WZ), Reid Technique, or equivalent interviewing certification preferred.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement background a plus.
  • Familiarity with CTPAT, TAPA, or SOC-related security requirements a plus.

Leadership Profile

  • A builder and developer of people — energized by growing a team, not just managing one.
  • Highly credible with frontline associates and site operations leaders; earns trust through presence and follow-through.
  • Capable of holding the line on standards while maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with operations partners.
  • Analytical and data-driven; able to translate metrics into clear narratives and actionable plans for regional and executive audiences.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity — able to triage competing priorities, escalate appropriately, and keep the team focused under pressure.
  • Strong written and verbal communicator; able to represent the region in enterprise forums and deliver clear guidance to site teams.

Nortek Data Center Cooling builds the systems that keep modern data centers running — from liquid cooling to large‑scale air solutions. Our work supports some of the world’s most demanding AI and hyperscale environments, and we solve those challenges with engineering depth and practical execution.

We keep things simple here. We communicate early, stay close to the details, and follow through. When issues come up, we address them directly, not with layers of process. Customers count on us because we do what we say and we keep projects moving.


Our culture is hands‑on and collaborative. People take ownership, move quickly, and help each other. If you like working with teammates who are straightforward and accountable, you’ll feel at home.

Nortek Data Center Cooling. is an equal employment opportunity employer and all qualiﬁed applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a qualiﬁed individual with a disability or any other characteristic protected by law.


Nortek Data Center Cooling offers comprehensive compensation and benefits package. Our benefits package includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life, STD, LTD, FSA, HAS and 401(k) Plan with company contributions. To apply, please visit our career site at .


Job Summary

The Metals & Fasteners Category Manager is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies across key direct material categories including carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, and industrial fasteners supporting Nortek Data Center Cooling's manufacturing operations. This role combines strategic category management with tactical execution, ensuring material availability, competitive cost structures, supplier performance, and supply chain continuity across multiple manufacturing locations.


The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of metals markets, fabrication processes, supplier management, and category strategy. This individual will leverage market intelligence, supplier partnerships, and cross-functional collaboration to drive cost reduction, support business growth, and ensure a resilient supply chain capable of supporting Nortek's expanding data center cooling business.

What You’ll Do

Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies for metals, fabricated components, and fastener categories.
  • Analyze commodity market trends, cost drivers, and industry indices, including CRU and other relevant market benchmarks, to support sourcing decisions and negotiations.
  • Build and maintain category strategies aligned with business objectives, supplier capabilities, and operational requirements.
  • Develop cost models, should-cost analyses, and forecasting tools to support procurement decisions.
  • Identify opportunities for cost reduction, supplier consolidation, and long-term value creation.
  • Manage the assigned category portfolio and maintain visibility to spend, pricing, and supplier performance metrics.

Supplier Identification & Management

  • Identify, evaluate, qualify, and develop strategic suppliers across metals fabrication, raw materials, and fastener categories.
  • Lead supplier negotiations covering pricing, lead times, service levels, inventory strategies, and capacity commitments.
  • Establish and maintain strong supplier relationships to ensure quality, delivery, responsiveness, and continuous improvement.
  • Monitor supplier performance using key performance indicators and implement corrective actions when necessary.
  • Evaluate supplier capacity and develop risk mitigation plans to support business continuity.
  • Support sourcing decisions related to direct-buy, distributor, and vendor-managed inventory (VMI) programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Design Optimization

  • Partner with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to support product cost, manufacturability, and supply continuity objectives.
  • Influence material selection and design-for-cost initiatives during new product development and product enhancement activities.
  • Recommend alternative materials, fabrication methods, and sourcing strategies that improve cost, quality, or lead time performance.
  • Support new supplier qualifications, product launches, and supplier transition projects.
  • Coordinate sourcing activities across multiple manufacturing locations to ensure alignment and standardization.

Supply Chain Execution & Operational Support

  • Collaborate with Planning, Operations, and Procurement teams to ensure material availability supports production schedules and customer commitments.
  • Manage supplier lead times, inventory strategies, and replenishment programs to balance supply continuity and working capital objectives.
  • Support multi-site inventory optimization initiatives.
  • Track, analyze, and report category spend, savings performance, supplier scorecards, and supply chain metrics.
  • Serve as a key escalation point for supplier-related delivery, capacity, and performance issues.

Risk Management, Compliance & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and maintain supplier risk assessments and contingency plans for critical materials and suppliers.
  • Ensure compliance with trade regulations, company sourcing policies, and applicable procurement standards.
  • Support sustainability, ethical sourcing, and supplier diversity initiatives where applicable.
  • Drive continuous improvement projects focused on cost reduction, supplier performance, inventory optimization, and process standardization.
  • Collaborate with Logistics, Quality, and Operations teams to strengthen end-to-end supply chain performance.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, Materials Science, Operations Management, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of sourcing, procurement, or category management experience within a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Experience sourcing metals, fabricated components, industrial hardware, fasteners, or related direct material categories.
  • Strong understanding of commodity markets, metals pricing, fabrication processes, and cost drivers.
  • Experience developing category strategies, supplier negotiations, and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and collaborate effectively with technical teams.
  • Experience managing large SKU portfolios and complex supplier networks.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems, supplier performance management tools, and Microsoft Office applications.

Preferred

  • MBA or advanced degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, or Business.
  • Experience sourcing across carbon steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, and industrial fastener categories.
  • Familiarity with CRU indices, commodity forecasting, and should-cost modeling.
  • Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.
  • Knowledge of fabrication processes including laser cutting, punching, machining, welding, forming, and finishing.
  • Experience with supplier quality, global sourcing, trade compliance, and sustainability programs.
  • Background in HVAC, data center infrastructure, industrial equipment, or engineered products manufacturing.

Why Join Nortek DCC

  • Play an important role on a growing team
  • Contribute to a company helping power the next generation of AI‑ready data centers
  • Work in an environment with meaningful growth opportunities

Receptionist (Construction)

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a confident, organized, and customer-focused Remote Receptionist to support a construction business focused on roofing and custom home services.

This is a highly phone-based role combining inbound lead response, outbound follow-up, cold calling, appointment booking, and call tracking. You’ll be one of the first points of contact for potential customers, helping turn inquiries into booked consultations while ensuring every interaction is properly documented.

What You’ll Own

Inbound Lead Response

  • Receive and handle calls from leads who have submitted forms through the company website.
  • Qualify their interest and understand their needs.
  • Move qualified leads toward a booked appointment with the appropriate team member.

Outbound Lead Follow-Up

  • Proactively call prospects who have expressed interest but have not yet converted.
  • Keep the pipeline warm through consistent follow-up.
  • Reduce drop-off between initial inquiry and consultation.

Cold Calling

  • Conduct structured outbound cold calling campaigns.
  • Generate new interest in roofing and custom home services.
  • Follow established scripts while adapting naturally to live conversations.

Appointment Booking

  • Schedule consultations and site visits accurately.
  • Coordinate availability with the appropriate team members.
  • Avoid double-bookings and missed opportunities.

Call Tracking & Notes

  • Log every call, outcome, and follow-up action clearly.
  • Keep lead records accurate and up to date.
  • Ensure the team always has a current view of where each lead stands.

Professional Brand Representation

  • Serve as the first voice many customers hear.
  • Communicate warmly, clearly, and professionally.
  • Speak confidently about the company's roofing and custom home offerings.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Proven experience in a receptionist, call center, customer service, or inside sales role with a significant phone-based component.
  • Experience handling both inbound and outbound calls confidently.
  • Ability to conduct cold calls without heavy supervision.
  • Strong spoken and written English fluency.
  • Clear pronunciation and strong active listening skills.
  • Ability to keep callers engaged and conversations on track.
  • Comfortable using scheduling or CRM tools to log calls and manage appointments.
  • Specific platform experience is a plus.
  • Reliable home office setup with stable internet, a quality headset, and a quiet calling environment.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You remain calm and professional when calls become challenging.
  • You are comfortable handling rejection and staying consistent during cold calling.
  • You take ownership of lead follow-up rather than waiting to be reminded.
  • You proactively flag unusual or important customer situations to the internal team.
  • You are organized and consistently document every interaction.
  • You can work independently while maintaining close communication with the team.

What Success Looks Like

  • New website leads are contacted promptly and professionally.
  • Qualified prospects are effectively moved toward booked appointments.
  • Follow-up leads remain warm and receive consistent outreach.
  • Cold calling generates new conversations and interest.
  • Appointments are scheduled accurately without double-bookings or missed opportunities.
  • Every call and follow-up action is properly documented.
  • The team has a clear, up-to-date view of the lead pipeline.
  • Customers receive a professional and positive first impression of the company.

Typical Day

Your day revolves around the phone. You’ll start by reviewing new form submissions and prioritizing callback attempts for fresh leads.

As calls come in, you’ll qualify callers, answer basic questions about roofing projects and custom home builds, and schedule appointments on the calendar.

Between inbound calls, you’ll run outbound sessions, following up with leads that have gone cold and working through cold calling lists to open new conversations.

You’ll log every interaction as you go, ensuring the team has a live picture of the pipeline.

The role is largely independent, but you’ll stay in close communication with the internal team to flag hot leads, reschedule appointments, and surface anything that requires their attention.

Interview Process

  1. Recruiter Screening
  2. Client Interview
  3. Final Selection

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, we believe a clear and reliable software experience matters for everyone interacting with the platform. We value people who communicate thoughtfully, pay attention to details, solve problems, and understand when an issue needs to be handled by a specialized team.

About the Role

We're looking for a Patient Experience Associate to support non-clinical patient interactions within Bask Health's telehealth platform, subject to the approved scope of our patient support operations.

This role is designed for someone who enjoys helping people, communicates clearly, and can work through software-related questions with patience and attention to detail.

You'll help patients navigate supported platform experiences, understand where to find information, and resolve routine non-clinical issues.

You'll provide clear, accurate assistance while recognizing when a question requires a licensed healthcare professional, pharmacy team, technical specialist, or other authorized contact.

Bask Health provides software that helps businesses launch and manage direct-to-consumer telehealth services.

The platform includes patient questionnaires, checkout experiences, account-related workflows, and connections to clinical and pharmacy operations.

You'll develop a working understanding of these software experiences so you can help users navigate them appropriately.

You'll assist with routine questions about accessing supported platform features and completing non-clinical steps.

You'll help identify situations where a patient is unable to proceed through an expected platform workflow.

You'll gather relevant details about reported software issues and document them accurately.

You'll troubleshoot basic navigation and access problems using approved procedures.

You'll avoid providing instructions that fall outside the responsibilities or authorization of the patient experience team.

You'll communicate with patients through approved support channels, which may include email, chat, or other systems selected by Bask Health.

You'll provide clear explanations without using unnecessary technical language.

You'll remain professional and patient when assisting people who may be frustrated or confused.

You'll take time to understand the issue before recommending an approved next step.

You'll help patients understand what information or action is needed to resolve a non-clinical platform problem.

You'll maintain accurate records of interactions, reported issues, and follow-up commitments.

You'll follow established procedures for documenting requests and escalating unresolved concerns.

You'll recognize when an issue cannot be resolved through standard troubleshooting.

You'll coordinate with technical support or engineering teams when a platform issue requires additional investigation.

You'll provide relevant information to technical teams so they can investigate problems efficiently.

You'll follow up on open issues according to approved service procedures.

You'll help ensure patients receive accurate updates when a non-clinical issue is being addressed.

You'll work with customer success or merchant support teams when an issue involves a merchant's platform configuration or account responsibilities.

You'll follow established ownership boundaries so requests are directed to the correct organization or team.

You'll refer those questions to the appropriate licensed or authorized healthcare professional.

You'll recognize when a question involves medication preparation, dispensing, fulfillment, or pharmacy-specific decisions.

You'll route those matters to the appropriate pharmacy or authorized support channel.

You'll never provide medical advice, recommend medications, interpret clinical information, or make treatment decisions.

You'll avoid making promises about clinical approval, prescription outcomes, medication availability, or fulfillment timelines unless approved information explicitly supports the communication.

You'll follow appropriate privacy, security, and information-handling procedures.

You'll access and share only the information necessary and authorized for your responsibilities.

You'll follow approved identity verification procedures before discussing account-specific information.

You'll use designated systems and communication channels when handling sensitive information.

You'll report suspected privacy or security concerns through established internal procedures.

You'll help identify recurring platform issues that create confusion or prevent patients from completing expected steps.

You'll document common questions and share relevant patterns with the appropriate internal teams.

You'll contribute suggestions for improving patient-facing instructions and support resources.

You'll organize your work to manage multiple conversations and follow-up tasks.

You'll prioritize urgent issues according to established procedures and escalation guidelines.

You'll take responsibility for completing assigned tasks and communicating when additional help is needed.

You'll ask questions when procedures are unclear rather than guessing about sensitive matters.

You'll help create a supportive experience for people who may be unfamiliar with telehealth software.

You'll maintain a professional tone in written and verbal communication.

You'll be comfortable learning new tools and adapting as platform workflows evolve.

You'll work with team members across departments to make sure issues reach the right people.

You'll support continuous improvement by sharing feedback about recurring problems and inefficient processes.

You'll contribute to an environment that values accountability, accuracy, empathy, and clear communication.

We're looking for someone with customer-facing support experience, strong communication skills, and the ability to follow established procedures.

You don't need to be a medical professional for this proposed role, and you will not be responsible for providing clinical advice.

Experience with healthcare technology or patient services would be helpful, but strong customer support experience and the ability to learn software workflows are also valuable.

Success in this role means helping patients navigate approved non-clinical workflows, resolving routine issues accurately, escalating specialized concerns appropriately, and contributing to a consistent, reliable platform experience.

  • Help patients navigate supported platform workflows.

  • Maintain a patient, respectful, and detail-oriented approach.
  • Take ownership of assigned requests through resolution or appropriate handoff.

Requirements

jobs.title: Performance Modeling Engineer, AI Inference Deployments (Senior/Principal)
jobs.excerpt: About Positron AI Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference.
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

As a Senior Performance Modeling Engineer, you will own the tools that tell customers how a model will run on Positron hardware at scale: how many chips it needs, what throughput and latency it will deliver, and how that compares with GPUs and other accelerators. You will work directly with customers, product, and our chip modeling team to turn deployment questions into quantified answers they can plan against.

The work spans analytical modeling, simulation, and real hardware measurements. You will build deployment-level models on top of our chip performance simulators, validate them against hardware, and package the results so customers can run them on their own. We are hiring two engineers for this work: one will take primary responsibility for the modeling architecture, and the other for per-model deployment studies and the customer-facing tool.

Key Responsibilities

Customer and Product Partnership

  • Partner with customers and product to turn deployment questions into focused studies with clear assumptions, options, metrics, and recommendations.
  • Run apples-to-apples comparisons of the same deployment on competitor hardware and explain what drives the difference.
  • Design and deliver a standalone performance-estimation tool that customers can run on their own workloads.

Deployment and System Modeling

  • Model deployment topologies for large-scale inference, including tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallelism, batching, context length, and mixed Positron-plus-GPU configurations.
  • Model the network and system layer, including interconnect latency and bandwidth, redundancy, and how these bound throughput as chip count grows.
  • Develop and extend analytical and simulation-based deployment models that consume our chip performance simulator, so every estimate traces back to one shared hardware model.

Validation and Calibration

  • Validate projections against measured hardware runs and keep models calibrated as chips, software, and workloads evolve.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in performance modeling, capacity planning, or systems architecture for large-scale AI inference, HPC, or data-center systems.
  • Demonstrated experience building analytical or queueing performance models and calibrating them against measured systems.
  • Deep understanding of LLM inference at the systems level, including prefill versus decode, KV cache, parallelism strategies, mixture-of-experts routing, batching, time-to-first-token, and tokens per second.
  • A solid working knowledge of data-center networking (latency, bandwidth, and topology) and GPU performance characteristics.
  • Comfort working from incomplete information, stating assumptions explicitly, and delivering an answer with error bars rather than waiting for certainty.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for analysis, experiments, and visualization.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain a sizing result, what drives it, and how much to trust it to both engineers and customers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience sizing or benchmarking inference deployments across many accelerators in production.
  • A track record of building customer-facing performance or TCO tools.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • Your models will directly shape how customers size, plan, and buy frontier-scale inference deployments, and how Positron's hardware is positioned against GPUs and other accelerators.
  • You will work at the intersection of silicon, systems, and customers, with direct access to our chip simulators, real hardware measurements, and the engineers building Asimov and Titan.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role for Senior: $220,000 – $270,000, for Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available

Time off and flexibility

  • Unlimited paid time off; we encourage everyone to truly unplug and recharge
  • 13 paid company holidays
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every bullet, we'd still love to hear from you.
