jobs.excerpt: As a Security Engineer at Stacks Labs, you'll work with the CTO to help building secure systems, including the sBTC signer network, the Stacks node, our smart contracts, and the infrastructure and release pipeline that ship them.
jobs.description:
As a Security Engineer at Stacks Labs, you'll work with the CTO to help building secure systems, including the sBTC signer network, the Stacks node, our smart contracts, and the infrastructure and release pipeline that ship them.

You'll operate autonomously in a fully remote role, embedded with a globally distributed engineering team. This is a hands-on role for someone who would rather find and fix the bug instead of writing a slide about it.

Outcomes You'll Drive

  • We find our vulnerabilities before anyone else does
    You hunt through code, infrastructure, and deployments with an attacker's mindset. The things you find get triaged, remediated, fixed.
  • Security that ships as code
    Your work produces pull requests, hardened configs, detection rules, and tests. Engineers see you as someone who makes their systems better, not someone who slows them down.
  • A hardened perimeter where it matters
    Key custody, secrets management, access control, CI/CD, and the software supply chain are locked down against the realistic threats to a system securing crypto-assets.
  • An AI-augmented security practice
    LLMs and coding agents multiply your reach across code review, fuzzing, triage, and log analysis. You know exactly where they help, where they lie, and how to build systems that leverage them to scale things up.
  • Calm, rehearsed incident response
    When something goes wrong there's a playbook, a clear owner, and a blameless postmortem that leaves the system stronger than before.

What You'll Do

Offense

  • Threat model and attack our software, infrastructure, and contracts. Write exploits against our own systems before adversaries do.
  • Build and run fuzzing, property-based, and adversarial test harnesses.
  • Run internal red-team exercises and coordinate external audits and bug bounty programs, triaging and validating what comes back.

Defense

  • Detection and monitoring: what does "compromised" look like, and how do we know within minutes rather than days?
  • Harden hosts, CI/CD, and the software supply chain. Audit dependencies and design reproducible builds and signed/attested releases.
  • Support incident response and post-incident reviews.

Engineering & Tooling

  • Review security-sensitive PRs across the codebase and pair with engineers on secure design.
  • Build AI-driven security tooling: agents for code review and dependency triage, LLM-assisted log analysis, automated first-pass audits of new contracts and integrations.
  • Write clear, actionable findings and advisories for internal teams, external signers, and partners.

What We're Looking For

  • Security is what you do for fun, not just for work. CTFs, bug bounties, side research, reading advisories at breakfast.
  • 5+ years in software engineering and ****a meaningful portion of it in security. Red team, blue team, appsec, detection engineering, or security research.
  • Solid programming foundation. You read and write production code (Rust, Go, C, TypeScript, Python, or similar), and you understand systems, networking, and cryptography.
  • Hands-on offensive or defensive experience: exploit development, pentesting, incident response, detection engineering, or hardening production systems.
  • Pragmatism. You measure yourself in closed attack paths and shipped fixes. You know risk matrices exist, but you don't lead with them.
  • Fluency with AI tooling. You use LLMs and coding agents daily in security work, you've built something with them, and you have grounded opinions about their failure modes.
  • Strong written communication. Findings, advisories, and design reviews that people actually read and act on.
  • Comfort working remotely and autonomously across time zones.

Nice to Have

  • Expertise in Rust, our primary language.
  • Bitcoin protocol internals, or experience auditing smart contracts (Clarity, Solidity, or similar).
  • Threshold signatures, MPC, or applied cryptography.
  • Security of distributed systems and consensus protocols.
  • Cloud and infrastructure security.
  • Experience building AI agents for security workflows, or securing systems that integrate LLMs.
  • A public track record: CVEs, published research, notable CTF placings, or bug bounty history.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation including $160,000-$200,000 USD base salary.
  • Stacks (STX) tokens - STX is the native cryptocurrency of the Stacks network.
  • Comprehensive health coverage and free life and disability insurance.
  • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave to support you through one of life's biggest transitions.
  • Monthly stipends for your home office or co-working space of choice.
  • Annual learning and development stipend to keep growing your skills.
  • An open vacation policy, take the days you need when you need.
  • 401(k) with a 3% match.
  • A high-ownership role shaping some of the most critical infrastructure in the Stacks ecosystem.
  • A fast-moving, focused team where strong engineering judgment is valued and where your work will ship quickly and visibly.
  • The chance to define engineering standards for one of the most ambitious Bitcoin L2 ecosystems, shaping how Bitcoin moves in and out of smart contracts.
  • A remote-first culture with flexibility, autonomy, and deep collaboration with product and engineering.

Job Description:

  • Own kernel driver signing: You run the end-to-end signing process for our Windows kernel drivers, including EV code signing, Microsoft Partner Center attestation, and HLK/WHQL submissions where needed. You keep the pipeline compliant with Microsoft’s driver signing requirements as they change.
  • Package for the enterprise: You build and maintain MSI, MSIX, and Win32 (.intunewin) packages for Intune deployment. You define install and uninstall logic, detection rules, dependencies, silent installs, and upgrade paths that IT teams can roll out to thousands of devices without a single support ticket.
  • Manage the certificate lifecycle: You own every certificate the product relies on: code signing, driver signing, root and intermediate certificates for TLS inspection, and device and service certificates. You handle issuance, secure storage in HSMs or key vaults, distribution, rotation, renewal, and revocation, with zero surprise expiries.
  • Automate signing and release: You integrate signing and packaging into CI/CD so every release is signed, versioned, and reproducible. No manual steps on someone’s laptop and no private keys in places they should not be.
  • Enable customer deployments: You write the deployment guides, Intune configuration profiles, and certificate trust policies that customer IT teams follow. You join calls with their endpoint teams to troubleshoot rollouts when needed.
  • Own reliability in the field: You track deployment success rates, failed installs, and signing or trust errors across the install base, and you fix root causes, not symptoms.

Requirements

  • Seasoned Windows systems engineer: 5+ years of experience in Windows systems engineering, endpoint engineering, or build and release for Windows software. You know the Windows installer stack, services, the registry, and the certificate stores inside out.
  • Driver signing experience: You have signed and shipped Windows kernel drivers in production through Microsoft’s attestation or WHQL process. You understand EV certificates, cross-signing history, and what Secure Boot and HVCI require.
  • Hands-on Intune packaging: You have packaged and deployed software through Microsoft Intune at enterprise scale, including Win32 apps, MSI/MSIX, detection rules, and configuration profiles. SCCM/MECM experience is a plus.
  • PKI and certificate management: You have managed certificate lifecycles in production, using tools such as Azure Key Vault, HSMs, internal CAs, or certificate management platforms. You can explain a chain of trust to a developer and to a customer’s security team.
  • Automation mindset: You script with PowerShell and have built signing or packaging steps into CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps.
  • Clear communicator: You can walk a US enterprise IT team through a deployment in plain English, and you write documentation people actually follow.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. You will be AI fluent and know how AI influences engineering and DevOps

jobs.excerpt: Role summary The Practice Director, SDLC leads the development and evolution of Valiantys’ North American Software Development Life Cycle practice.
jobs.description:
Role summary
The Practice Director, SDLC leads the development and evolution of Valiantys’ North American Software Development Life Cycle practice. The role helps clients modernize and orchestrate the full flow of delivering and operating software—from discovery and planning through design, implementation, testing, deployment and ongoing maintenance. It combines practice leadership, delivery excellence, commercial leadership and solution ownership. A consultative mindset is essential: uncovering business and industry context, shaping options into practical roadmaps, and connecting technical choices to measurable outcomes. The role is focused on North American execution and operates in a global matrix, aligning regional priorities with the direction set by the Global Head of Practice.
Responsibilities
Practice leadership
• Act as the Global Head of Practice’s regional delegate, representing Valiantys in strategic client, partner and Atlassian interactions and embedding the global SDLC strategy in North America.
• Build the regional practice around end-to-end software delivery transformation, spanning engineering workflows, DevOps practices, governance, quality, delivery speed and measurable business outcomes.
• Serve as the regional SDLC solution authority, combining strong Atlassian platform knowledge with a broad view of complementary engineering and DevOps technologies, and mobilizing deep specialist expertise where needed.
• Maintain a current view of established and emerging engineering and DevOps technologies and leading practices, including Atlassian products (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Jira Service Management and Rovo), complementary tools such as Xray and SonarQube, and DX and similar capabilities for engineering metrics and insights. Assess how these capabilities align and integrate with Atlassian and client environments, including evolving AI capabilities.
• Keep the practice skills matrix, capability plans and enablement priorities current across SDLC transformation, platforms, delivery and AI-enabled ways of working.
• Foster a collaborative, high-performance practice culture that shares field insight, leading practices and lessons learned to improve client value and Valiantys revenue.
• Ensure approved practice and company methods, governance and tools are applied consistently across North America.
• Own the regional SDLC Practice shadow P&L, including investment in solution-component development and practice enablement. Partner with the Global Head of Practice and Head of Delivery to clarify regional versus global ownership of training, certification, enablement and solution-development investments, and surface gaps where ownership is not defined.
Delivery
• Define and oversee delivery approaches for complex or high-impact SDLC transformation engagements, ensuring alignment with client outcomes, technical feasibility, operating-model needs, Valiantys standards and leading practices.
• Lead consultative discovery with client executives and delivery teams, translating ambiguous business needs into target operating models, SDLC roadmaps, solution architectures and phased plans with measurable outcomes.
• Bring expertise in one or more client domains, particularly complex or regulated environments, and adapt SDLC transformation to industry-specific business models and constraints, including security, compliance and adoption needs.
• Act as a senior advisor to strategic clients, helping leaders connect investment in engineering and DevOps improvement to measurable business outcomes.
• Provide design assurance across the full software delivery lifecycle, including discovery, planning, feasibility, system design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance, with attention to security, compliance, resilience, observability, scalability, operational readiness and cost effectiveness.
• Oversee key deliverables and delivery risks where appropriate, including adoption, governance, quality and operating-model considerations that extend beyond a tooling implementation. Assess the delivery, support and maintenance implications of AI-enabled solutions, including clear ownership and appropriate lifecycle plans.
• Guide client onboarding, enablement and iterative improvement so transformed SDLC capabilities are adopted across technical teams and deliver their intended business value.
• Support the Delivery Management team in forecasting the skills and capacity required for the regional practice.
• Partner with practice and delivery leadership on plans for training, certifications, internal enablement and solution development, in line with the agreed practice investment model.
Sales support
• Support sales on complex or large-scale SDLC opportunities, providing credible executive and technical leadership while ensuring feasibility and alignment with practice strategy.
• Run regular pipeline reviews and deal clinics to identify where repeatable offerings should be used and where a tailored solution is justified.
• Guide sales teams on the value, scope and appropriate use of the SDLC solution catalogue, including AI-enabled capabilities where they provide an evidenced client benefit.
• Contribute to the validation of statements of work, estimates and delivery models to support accurate scoping, commercial discipline and delivery feasibility.
• Work with Marketing, Alliances and the Transformation practice (Tx) on SDLC go-to-market strategy, thought leadership, case studies and market messages.
Product and solution ownership
• Collaborate with the Head of Solutions and Global Head of Practice to manage the lifecycle of SDLC solutions, accelerators and training offers from idea through retirement.
• Lead regional development of repeatable solution components for the full delivery-project lifecycle, including discovery materials, repeatable roadmaps and delivery-ready project assets and deliverables.
• Develop repeatable SDLC transformation components, including AI-enabled patterns that strengthen planning, knowledge flow, engineering productivity, quality, service operations or governance; account for their design, delivery, support and maintenance implications.
• Act as design authority for repeatable solution components, ensuring they support product marketing, delivery quality, sales efficiency and measurable client outcomes.
• Enable Practice consultants, sales and delivery teams to use approved components effectively and consistently.
• Own the regional IP development lifecycle, ensuring investments align with the strategic direction of the practice and can be scaled or reused.
• Ensure delivery lessons and client evidence inform continuous improvement of offerings, methods and enablement.
• Coordinate with other practices to remove duplication and close gaps across Valiantys’ solution portfolio.
Your team and partners
• Head of Delivery, North America — line manager
• Global Head of Practice — dotted-line manager
• Principal Consultants and other Practice team members, where applicable
• Product Owners and Head of Solutions
• Delivery Management team
• Sales, Marketing and Alliances teams, including the Transformation practice (Tx)
• People and Culture team
• Global Partner Manager and strategic partners

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!
